company: Helsing builds AI software and systems for defense applications, including electronic warfare, autonomy, battlefield decision support, AI-enabled strike drones and autonomous platforms. It sells principally to governments and defense partners, integrating software with military hardware from companies such as Saab and Rheinmetall.

Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine reshaped European defense priorities and accelerated demand for sovereign defense technology. Helsing's July 2026 Series E raised $1.8B at an $18.0B valuation, following a €600M Series D in June 2025. Multiples records $502M of revenue alongside the Series E, implying a 35.9× valuation-to-revenue multiple.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Helsing sits at the intersection of European rearmament and AI-enabled defense. The $18.0B valuation implies a 35.9× multiple on Multiples-recorded revenue, so the investment case depends on converting defense demand into repeatable procurement, deployments and durable software economics.

changed.text: Helsing is founded to apply artificial intelligence to European defense and security.
Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine makes European defense readiness and sovereign technology a more urgent priority.
A €600M Series D values Helsing at a reported €12B.
A $1.8B Series E raises the reported valuation to $18.0B; Multiples records $502M of revenue alongside the round.

takeaways: Helsing is a private-market defense AI company operating across electronic warfare, autonomy and battlefield software.
Russia's invasion of Ukraine accelerated European demand for sovereign defense technology and sharpened the company's strategic relevance.
The $18.0B valuation implies a 35.9× multiple on the $502M of revenue recorded by Multiples alongside the Series E.
The key next evidence is whether Helsing can translate defense demand into repeatable procurement, deployments and durable software economics.
